{{Short description|Irish mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}

'''Robert William Genese''' (1848, Dublin – 1928) was an Irish mathematician whose career was spent in Wales.

==Early life and education==
Genese was born on [[Westland Row]] a street on the south side of Dublin on 8 May 1848. From [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]] of the [[University of Cambridge]], Genese received in 1871 his bachelor's degree (with rank eighth [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Wrangler]] in the [[Tripos]]) and in 1874 his master's degree.

==Professional life==
Following an unsuccessful application for the Chair of Mathematics at [[Aberystwyth University|Aberystwyth]] in 1872, he taught at the Training College in [[Carmarthen]]. He finally secured the professorship at Aberystwyth in 1879, and held it until 1919. Along the way his title became Professor of Mathematics and Astronomy.<ref name=Aberystwyth>''[https://www.llgc.org.uk/fileadmin/fileadmin/docs_gwefan/amdanom_ni/cylchgrawn_llgc/cgr_erth_XXXVrh1_2010_4.pdf The College by the Sea’ and its photographs]'' a history of The [[University College of Wales]], [[Aberystwyth]]</ref>
 
Genese introduced into the United Kingdom the ideas of [[Hermann Grassmann]] (advancing the use of vector analysis). In his 1941 book ''The calculus of extensions'', [[Henry Forder]] published numerous examples in vector analysis taken from Genese's posthumous notes. (Genese's notes were left to the [[Mathematical Association]] and then given in 1929 to Forder by [[Eric Harold Neville|E. H. Neville]].)<ref>{{cite book|author=Forder, Henry George|chapter=Preface, page v|title=The Calculus of Extension, including examples by Robert William Genese|year=1941|publisher=University of Cambridge Press|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yyU9AAAAIAAJ}}</ref>

Genese was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1904 in [[Heidelberg]] with talk ''On some useful theorems in the continued multiplication of a regressive product in real four-point space''<ref>[https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0004.001;view=1up;seq=399 ''On some useful theorems in the continued multiplication of a regressive product in real four-point space''], Proceedings of the ICM in 1904, Heidelberg</ref> and in 1908 in Rome with talk ''The method of reciprocal polars applied to forces in space''.

==Selected publications==
*"Suggestions for the Practical Treatment of the Standard Cubic Equation, and a Contribution to the Theory of Substitution." The Mathematical Gazette 9, no. 129 (1917): 65–69. {{doi|10.2307/3603498}}
*"On the Theory of the Plane Complex with Simple Geometrical and Kinematical Illustrations." The Mathematical Gazette 11, no. 164 (1923): 293–301. {{doi|10.2307/3603761}}
*"A Simple Exposition of Grassmann's Methods." The Mathematical Gazette 13, no. 189 (1927): 373–391. {{doi|10.2307/3604329}}
